title: The 10 Best Cordless Screwdrivers
subtitle: Rechargeable 4V to 8V power screwdrivers for furniture, outlets and small repairs, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A cordless screwdriver is a small, light power driver for the jobs where a drill is overkill: flat-pack furniture, switch plates, cabinet hinges, battery covers. Most run on a built-in 4V battery that charges over USB. We ranked 10 best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (adjustable torque, an LED, a pivoting or two-position grip and a bit set in the box). They run from about $25 to $140 for Milwaukee's M4 kit. For heavier driving, see our impact driver list.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

avoid.name: MQFORU Blue Cordless Electric Screwdriver Set, 3.7V Rechargeable, 47pcs Driver Bit Set (TY002)
avoid.flag: Listing names a different brand and contradicts its own specs
avoid.verdict: A budget kit whose listing can't keep its own name or numbers straight. The Amazon Basics by SKIL driver costs about $5 more, comes from a known maker and has three torque settings.
reasons: It's sold by the MQFORU store, but every bullet calls it a "MYMULIKE" screwdriver, so it's unclear who makes it or stands behind it.
The title says 3.7V; the spec table says 3.6V.
The spec table lists a 12 mm maximum chuck size on a driver that takes 1/4-inch (6.35 mm) hex bits.
The listing quotes a 3-to-5-hour recharge for a 1,300 mAh battery. The DEWALT recharges its 2Ah battery in 60 minutes.

buyers_guide.a: A cordless screwdriver is lighter, smaller and gentler: perfect for furniture, cover plates and hinges, where a drill can strip or snap small screws. For long wood screws, lag bolts or drilling holes, use a drill or impact driver.

A clutch stops the driver when the screw is snug, so you don't strip the head or crack particleboard. That matters most on flat-pack furniture and electronics. Drivers without settings need you to stop the trigger yourself.

buyers_guide.q: How much torque do I need?
buyers_guide.a: Most 4V screwdrivers deliver 20 to 45 in-lb, enough for furniture and hardware. If you drive 2-inch wood screws, look at the 8V ENERTWIST (88 in-lb) or step up to a drill.

Most here have a built-in battery that charges over USB, which is convenient but means waiting when it's flat. The Metabo HPT and Milwaukee kits come with two swappable batteries, so one can charge while you work.

buyers_guide.q: Do I need a pivoting handle?
buyers_guide.a: A pivoting or two-position handle lets you switch between a straight stick grip for reach and a pistol grip for push and control. It's most useful inside cabinets and behind appliances.
